answers.flag: The Route 53 documentation says that when every nonzero-weight record is unhealthy Route 53 considers the zero-weight records, so D (one new weight-0 alias to the S3 website) works and takes less effort than C; a careful candidate could defend C as the textbook failover-over-weighted pattern, and the key must be whichever the author intends; check that D's behavior is stated by a verified fact, or the pair is a trap in the other direction.

case.label: C
case.text: C also works: a failover alias with Evaluate Target Health on the weighted group fails over to the S3 website only when none of the weighted records is healthy. It is more work than D (rename, new alias, new failover pair), so only LEAST overhead separates them.

answers.flag: A CNAME on a non-apex name is functionally correct and has no setup cost; the key depends on the unstated pricing fact that alias queries to AWS resources are free.

case.text: app.example.com is a subdomain, so a CNAME to the ALB DNS name is valid and fixes the stale addresses just as well; it is excluded only if the reader knows that Route 53 charges for CNAME queries but not for alias queries to an ALB, which the stem hints only through 'MOST cost-effective'.
